top3.headline: DeepMind agents crack legacy RSA-1024 assumptions
top3.whyItMatters: Human-guided agents found padding forgery shortcuts and about 30× cheaper batch factoring on 1024-bit keys.

top3.headline: a16z: rebuild defense so you stop needing patches
top3.whyItMatters: AI-cheap exploits make live fixes and short-lived credentials the product, not faster patch cycles.

top3.headline: Builders measure why subagent handoffs fail
top3.whyItMatters: Lossy summary handoffs underperformed; most work may need serial retrieval or fresh sessions.

items.title: DeepMind agents find two legacy RSA-1024 weaknesses
items.takeaway: Human-guided agents found signature-padding forgery shortcuts and a batch NFS method about 30× cheaper per extra 1024-bit key; DeepMind says 2048-bit+ RSA stays safe.
items.soWhat: AI is now stress-testing crypto assumptions leaders still run in long-lived systems.

items.title: Nilay Patel: AI products do not justify local costs yet
items.takeaway: On The Vergecast after midterm data-center pushback, Nilay said agents are not real for how people want them, labs spend more than they make, and backlash ends only when products obviously help without ads.
items.soWhat: Leaders selling AI buildouts need product proof neighbors can see, not campaign spin.

items.title: a16z: rebuild defense in depth for machine speed
items.takeaway: Asaf Ezra and Steph Zhang argue AI-cheap exploits mean products should make patching unnecessary; they list six openings from live fixes to long-tail managed security.
items.soWhat: Security roadmaps that only accelerate patch SLAs will lose to AI-paced attackers.

items.title: Akai and Moog open paths for vibe-coded firmware mods
items.takeaway: inMusic will open-source device code, ship an SDK and reset paths, and run a Creator Lab at NAMM after vibe-coded mods forced the issue onto the roadmap in five weeks.
items.soWhat: Hardware brands that ignore AI mods now face open-source demands from their own users.

items.title: Meng To flags three.js portfolios pushed with Opus
items.takeaway: Meng To highlighted Brice Deguigne's interactive 3D portfolio (bricelab.dev) as proof of how far portfolio sites can go with three.js and Claude Opus 5.5.
items.soWhat: Design hiring bars now include AI-built interactive 3D craft, not static case-study pages.

items.title: Amazon rolls out texting for Alexa shopping
items.takeaway: US customers can message Amazon Alexa with product descriptions or photos, get recommendations, and let it order; invite group today, then millions more in coming weeks.
items.soWhat: Commerce agents are moving into SMS, where OpenAI Dot and DoorDash already compete.

items.title: Nathan Benaich: agents ran 12 expert interviews
items.takeaway: Benaich said his agents on lato.ai framed questions, found experts, ran 12 interviews in 2.5 days, updated beliefs, and refined the study from his State of AI talk.
items.soWhat: Quiet investors are testing agent loops that replace early diligence interview grunt work.

items.title: Protesters break into Microsoft Amsterdam data-center site
items.takeaway: About 100 Geef Tegengas protesters entered a Pure Data Centres site for three Microsoft towers, scaled a crane with a 'fuck AI' banner, amid a wider European protest week.
items.soWhat: Data-center siting risk is physical and political now, not only a grid or CapEx story.

items.title: Naval: be loved and hated, or merely tolerated
items.takeaway: Naval posted that you can be loved and hated, or merely liked and tolerated; the line drew more than 7.5k likes within hours.
items.soWhat: Investor taste still prizes sharp positioning over broad likability.

items.title: Alexander Yue: lossy subagent handoffs are a top failure
items.takeaway: On a 137k-token Opus 5.5 session, checkpoint forks and classic subagents both lagged a solo agent; he argues most work should be serial with retrieval or fresh parallel sessions.
items.soWhat: Agent org charts that delegate via summaries may burn cost without better outcomes.

items.title: Builders race to replace Conductor before Nov 20 shutdown
items.takeaway: After Meta set Conductor Cloud to shut Nov 20, Ryan Shea's alternatives list passed about 40 products; Garry Tan said Capy is a Conductor superset that 5×ed his efficiency.
items.soWhat: Agent orchestration state needs an exit path; a git clone alone will not migrate it.

items.title: arXiv: score compressed agent memory on global structure
items.takeaway: Paper 2611.08341 argues compression checks that only keep nearest neighbors miss consolidate/delete/compare needs; evaluate local fidelity L and global fidelity G far apart in memory.
items.soWhat: Memory compression that only preserves neighbors can break agent decisions that need contrast.
